# lambda__opensearch__s3: a presigned S3 URL generated by an in-function SDK names the public AWS S3 host, not an address the emulator serves

> _Note: this issue was identified against the code base at commit `44786d0c9f40e8c1d9dd84c42bcd4a9c51c55d07`. If you are an issue fixer working on this, the code base you are currently working in can have drifted, so you might need to trace the issue back to the current code base._

## Operation
Invoke

## Description
This issue carries 1 root cause, in the lambda__opensearch__s3 surface. It must be closed before submitting.

Cause 1 of 1: a Lambda function that uses its bundled AWS SDK to presign an S3 GET produces a URL whose host is the public AWS S3 endpoint instead of the endpoint the emulator is reached on, so the URL the emulator hands back cannot be fetched from the emulator at all. The function executes and returns a syntactically valid SigV4 presigned URL — the defect is the address the emulator announces inside it.

AWS: recorded behavior only (no Smithy member governs a presigned URL; it is produced client-side by the SDK from the client's resolved endpoint). Recorded: boto3's generate_presigned_url('get_object', Params={Bucket,Key}, ExpiresIn=300) inside a Lambda returns a URL for the S3 endpoint the function's SDK is configured with, signed with the execution role's credentials, and an external HTTP GET of that URL returns the object's bytes with 200. The requirement exercised here is that the host in the returned URL is the S3 endpoint in force for that client, and that a GET of the URL serves the object body.

Emulator: the Lambda's SDK is configured with the real AWS endpoint, so the function returns 'https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/<key>?x-id=GetObject&X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=.../s3/aws4_request&X-Amz-Date=...&X-Amz-Expires=300&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=...&X-Amz-Security-Token=...'. The harness's published-URL check refuses it: 'its host is not one of the emulator\'s own hosts; a customer of the emulator needs http(s)://<emulator host>:<port>/<resource path>, or http(s)://<own host>:<port>/<path> on a per-resource listener'. The URL therefore points at an address the emulator does not serve, and the subsequent GET can never reach the object.

Why: presigning is the standard way a Lambda hands an object to a caller it does not want to proxy (download links, upload tickets, pipeline hand-offs). Against the emulator every such URL points off the emulator: a client that follows it either leaves the emulated environment or fails to resolve/connect, and the object is unreachable even though the function, the role policy (s3:GetObject on the key) and the object itself are all correct. Any workflow whose next step is 'fetch the presigned URL' is dead.

Fix: the Lambda execution environment's SDK endpoint configuration — the runtime that Invoke starts must give the function an S3 (and generally per-service) endpoint pointing at the emulator's own address, e.g. by injecting the endpoint-URL environment the bundled SDK resolves, and the credentials it signs with must be ones the emulator's S3 front door accepts, so that a URL the function presigns is a URL the emulator serves. Related open issues that do NOT cover this (they concern Invoke not executing a package, the runtime's missing SDK/os members, and S3-notification delivery): 20261105T111951Z-lambda-opensearch-s3-the-lambda-python-runtime-has.md, 20261103T020000Z-lambda-opensearch-s3-invoke-execution-and-cloudformation-stack-causes.md, 20261107T173234Z-lambda-opensearch-s3-an-s3-event-notification-with.md.

## Evidence
Failing check: [mismatch] lambda__opensearch__s3.lambda-sdk-s3-presigned-url-generation-positive.
AssertionError: the emulator published https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/presign.txt?x-id=GetObject&X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=<access key>/<date>/us-west-2/s3/aws4_request&X-Amz-Date=<ts>&X-Amz-Expires=300&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=<sig>&X-Amz-Security-Token=<token>: its host is not one of the emulator's own hosts; a customer of the emulator needs http(s)://<emulator host:port>/<resource path>, or http(s)://<own host>:<port>/<path> on a per-resource listener.
Expected (AWS, recorded): the returned URL's host is the S3 endpoint the invoking environment resolves (for the emulator, one of its own hosts), and urllib GET of the URL returns 200 with the object body b'presigned-content-abc123'.
Actual (emulator): the URL's host is the public AWS endpoint 's3.<region>.amazonaws.com', an address the emulator does not serve, so the GET leg is unreachable. The access key, signature, date, token, bucket name and port in the quoted URL are per-run values, not requirements; the requirement is the host and the fetchability of the URL.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. s3.create_bucket(Bucket=<name>, CreateBucketConfiguration={'LocationConstraint': <region>}) and s3.put_object(Bucket=<name>, Key='presign.txt', Body=b'presigned-content-abc123').
2. iam.create_role(<lambda trust policy for lambda.amazonaws.com>), attach AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole and put_role_policy allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>/presign.txt.
3. lambda.create_function(Runtime='python3.12', Handler='lambda_function.handler', Role=<role arn>, Code={'ZipFile': zip of a handler that calls boto3.client('s3').generate_presigned_url('get_object', Params={'Bucket': event['bucket'], 'Key': event['key']}, ExpiresIn=300) and returns {'url': url}}); wait for State=='Active'.
4. lambda.invoke(FunctionName=<fn>, Payload=json {'bucket': <bucket>, 'key': 'presign.txt'}) and read result['url'].
5. Inspect the URL's host: the emulator returns 's3.<region>.amazonaws.com' instead of its own host, and an HTTP GET of the URL does not serve the object. Re-replay lambda__opensearch__s3.lambda-sdk-s3-presigned-url-generation-positive.
